$comment: Per-map engine resource figures, measured rather than derived, which the
content build copies into the content manifest so they live with the
This file is deliberately NOT a per-archive selection input. Every archive's
generated notice carries the SHA-256 of its own selection input - the root
recipe for the base, content/maps/<name>.json for a map - so a number added
there would move that archive's bytes and its immutable URL. A measurement
is not content, and it must not be able to move content.
It still enters the release identity: the content manifest records this
file's digest as the input 'arena-web-resource-measurements' and copies the
figures into its own artifact entries, and scripts/release_index.py checks

caveats: These are 64-bit native figures and the browser build is 32-bit, where hunk-resident structures holding pointers are smaller and the raw arrays are the same size, so the figure over-estimates.

An earlier note here said a map measured mid-session differs from a cold-start load by about 1.5 MB. The control below contradicts it and is the direct test: oa_pvomit read as the first map of a cold client and as the tenth gives the identical figure, which is also what the method predicts, because Hunk_Clear zeroes both marks and both tempHighwater values on every map load. The position of a map in a session is therefore not a caveat on these figures.

The figure is base-dependent: s_shaderText is Hunk_Alloc'd, so the base becoming the pack's shader authority moved every map by about 0.15 MB. A release that changes what the base carries must re-measure rather than carry these numbers forward.

The figure does not depend on how many archives are mounted. That follows from the base being the pack's shader authority - every scripts/*.shader is in the base and in no map archive, so the Hunk_Alloc'd s_shaderText is the same whatever map archives are present - and the control above measures it rather than deriving it. It is why a batch that only adds archives may carry the earlier figures forward unchanged, while the base-dependence caveat above still stands. Checked rather than inferred from one map: qcommon/files.c makes no permanent hunk allocation at all - its only hunk use is Hunk_AllocateTempMemory for one file's bytes, freed - and pak mounting allocates from the zone, which is an independent calloc rather than a slice of the hunk, so s_shaderText and its hash table are the only file-set-dependent hunk allocations in the tree.
method.peakHunkBytes: One native client per session on Xvfb inside the pinned WP5 toolchain image, driven over its own console: 'map <name>', bot_minplayers 3, then 'meminfo'. Hunk_Clear zeroes both marks and both tempHighwater values on every map load (ioq3 code/qcommon/common.c), so each report is that map's own figure. The value is 'total hunk in use' plus 'unused highwater'. Sound is off, matching the method the whole set was ranked with. The two sessions behind these figures are tied together by a control rather than by assumption: oa_pvomit was re-loaded on 2026-09-02 both as the first map of a cold client and as the tenth, against a mount of seventeen archives instead of the nine it was first measured with, and all three readings are the same 31441576 bytes.
